reconstruction.scope: Principal connected Boyana Church exterior: stone western annex, taller brick middle bay with south exterior stair/raised door, lower eastern church with rounded apse and curved roof crown, red ceramic gables and octagonal tiled drum/cap/cross. Arched blind brickwork is raised framing over closed wall, with narrow dark window proxies. Upper door has an actual shallow recess, jambs, soffit, threshold and supported landing. Unseen northern/eastern elevations, internal subdivisions are conservative reconstructions. No fresco copies, furnished interior, garden monuments or surrounding buildings.

Source map height 5m and one level are unqualified controls, not survey. South landing/door threshold 3.05m, actual 0.35m recess, stair proportions reconstructed. Heights, inventories, north/east faces, roof junctions, exact paving/step levels are unverified. No authored historic frescoes or furnished rooms. An additional ordinary eastern exterior photo shows the rounded brick apse and curved roof crown. The source map simplifies this as a rectangle: the added 1.45m apse projection and its 3.55m wall/4.05m roof are picture-led approximations, not surveyed map geometry. Only the owned parent is replaced; the added apse has its own occupied ground mask. Upper doorway back uses shared dark painted metal; triangle and quad brick UVs now use the same metric repeat.
